rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the future form can describe a past utterance when it is repeated; reports say the criticism had already been voiced when the verse came down.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار القفال أن هذا اللفظ وإن كان للمستقبل ظاهرا لكنه قد يستعمل في الماضي أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse predicts the criticism before it occurs, demonstrating knowledge of the unseen, easing its hurt, and placing the answer ready for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إذا أخبر عن ذلك قبل وقوعه ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fool cannot distinguish benefit from harm and abandons sound judgment; error in religion is more harmful than worldly error, so every unbeliever is foolish.
rows.anchor: من لا يميز بين ما له وعليه ، ويعدل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: They identify the critics as Jews, who expected the Prophet's agreement on the qibla to lead to full agreement; after the change they said he had returned to his forefathers' way.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد : هم اليهود ، وذلك لأنهم كانوا يأتسون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، البراء بن عازب، الحسن، الأصم
rows.claim: They identify the critics as Arab polytheists: in Mecca the Prophet faced Jerusalem, but after turning to the Kaaba in Medina they claimed he had returned to their way.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والبراء بن عازب والحسن والأصم ، إنهم مشركو العرب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the critics as hypocrites, who mocked the shift as arbitrary because no rational feature distinguished one direction from another; the name fools is especially associated with them.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنهم المنافقون وهو قول السدي ، وهؤلاء إنما ذكروا ذلك استهزاء

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Judge says the verse only establishes that some group made this remark, so a universal reading is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : المقصود من الآية بيان وقوع هذا الكلام منهم في الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural can include all unbelievers, as reason and 2:130 indicate; the Judge's point does not restrict that scope, and enemies naturally criticize whenever able, so likely all said it.
rows.anchor: بل الأقرب أن يكون الكل قد قال ذلك لأن الأعداء مجبولون على القدح والطعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walla ʿan means to turn someone away from something, unlike wallā ilā; the same usage appears in 8:16.
rows.anchor: ولاه عنه صرفه عنه وولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “what turned them?” is phrased to express mockery and astonishment.
rows.anchor: استفهام على جهة الاستهزاء والتعجب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The well-known, consensus interpretation is that unbelievers mocked the Prophet and believers when God changed their qibla from Jerusalem to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: المفسرين : أنه لما حولت القبلة إلى الكعبة من بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas dates the qibla change to nine or ten months after the migration.
rows.anchor: فعن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه بعد تسعة أشهر أو عشرة أشهر

rows.speaker: معاذ
rows.claim: Muadh dates the qibla change to thirteen months after the migration.
rows.anchor: وعن معاذ بعد ثلاثة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada dates the qibla change to sixteen months after the migration.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة بعد ستة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Bara ibn ʿAzib date the change to seventeen months after the migration; al-Razi says this is the most established report.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والبراء بن عازب بعد سبعة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another report places the change eighteen months after the Prophet's arrival.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم ثمانية عشر شهرا من مقدمه

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: Al-Waqidi says the qibla changed on Monday, the middle of Rajab, after seventeen months.
rows.anchor: قال الواقدي : صرفت القبلة يوم الاثنين النصف من رجب

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other reports date the change to two years after the migration.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل سنتان

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim proposes that “the qibla they had been on” means the fools' familiar Jewish and Christian directions; since they had not customarily prayed toward a set direction, the Prophet's facing the Kaaba surprised them, and God answers that east and west belong to Him.
rows.anchor: قول أب مسلم وهو أنه لما صح الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi accepts the reported shift from Jerusalem to the Kaaba; without the clear reports, Abu Muslim's alternative remains plausible.
rows.anchor: فإنه لولا الروايات الظاهرة لكان هذا القول محتملا والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibla names the direction a person faces; the word derives from facing or mutual encounter.
rows.anchor: القبلة هي الجهة التي يستقبلها الإنسان

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub notes the idiom “he has no qibla,” meaning a person has no direction or refuge to turn to.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب : يقولون في كلامهم ليس لفلان قبلة ، أي ليس له جهة

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation is reciprocal: when two people face one another, each is the other's qibla.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره : إذ تقابل الرجلان فكل واحد منهما قبلة للآخر

rows.speaker: بعض المحدثين
rows.claim: A poetic line uses qibla for the direction or refuge toward which one turns.
rows.anchor: جعلت مأواك لي قرارا … وقبلة حيثما لجأت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first answer to the objection is that every direction belongs to God; none is inherently a qibla, and a direction becomes one only by God's designation, so changing it is unobjectionable.
rows.anchor: فلا يستحق شيء منها لذاته أن يكون قبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi frames two questions: why God initially designated a qibla and why He later changed it.
rows.anchor: قلنا : أما المسألة الأولى ففيها الخلاف الشديد بين أهل السنة والمعتزلة

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Sunnis hold that God's rulings need not be explained by purposes; if a purpose benefits God, He would be deficient, while if benefit is irrelevant to Him it cannot motivate the act.
rows.anchor: أما أهل السنة فإنهم يقولون : لا يجب تعليل أحكام الله تعالى ألبتة

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: They argue that if God can achieve a goal without an intermediary, using the intermediary is futile; if He cannot, that implies incapacity.
rows.anchor: كان توسط تلك الواسطة عبثا

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: They argue that an eternal purpose would entail an eternal act, while a created purpose requires another purpose, leading to circularity or an infinite regress.
rows.anchor: توقف إحداثه على غرض آخر ، ولزم الدور أو التسلسل وهو محال

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: They argue that explaining why the world began at a particular time by a special wisdom only repeats the question of why that wisdom arose then; either case calls for a further determiner or none.
rows.anchor: كان طلب العلة في أنه لم حصلت تلك الحكمة في ذلك الوقت دون سائر الأوقات كطلب العلة

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: They argue that all good and evil, faith and unbelief, obedience and sin occur by God's power and will, which rules out a purpose that returns to the servant in creating unbelief and eternally punishing it.
rows.anchor: واقع بقدرة الله تعالى وإرادته

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: They argue that God's eternal will either acts contingently, requiring another cause and regress, or necessarily, in which case it needs no cause.
rows.anchor: إما أن يكون جائزا أو وجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi concludes that God's acts proceed from divinity, power, and sovereignty; the verse grounds abrogation in His ownership of east and west, not in wisdom as the Muʿtazila say.
rows.anchor: والملك يرجع حاصله إلى القدرة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that a wise God cannot act without purposes; all acts and rulings have wisdom, sometimes evident and sometimes hidden, so the qibla change may have concealed benefits and does not discredit Islam.
rows.anchor: أما المعتزلة فقد قالوا : لما دلت الدلائل على أنه تعالى حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi cautions that proposed wisdoms for the qibla are not conclusive proofs but possibilities.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أمثال هذه المباحث لا تكون قطعية ، بل غايتها أن تكون أمورا احتمالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fixed direction gives imagination a concrete form to help the intellect grasp abstractions, like an engineer's diagram; facing the qibla resembles facing a king, while recitation praises him and bowing and prostration serve him.
rows.anchor: فاستقبال القبلة في الصلاة يجري مجرى كونه مستقبلا للملك لا معرضا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer seeks presence of heart, supported by stillness and avoiding distraction; keeping one direction helps, especially if that direction is regarded as honorable.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يتأتى إلا إذا بقي في جميع صلاته مستقبلا لجهة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shared direction promotes harmony among believers, a blessing named in 5:7; different directions could make them appear divided in worship.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى يحب الموافقة والألفة بين المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Kaaba God's house and believers His servants honors both; the worshipper faces God's house physically and God with the heart.
rows.anchor: يا مؤمن أنت عبدي ، والكعبة بيتي

rows.speaker: بعض المشايخ
rows.claim: Some shaykhs say Jews faced their qibla because Moses was called from the western side (28:44), Christians faced west because Gabriel came to Mary from the east (19:16), while Muslims face the Kaaba, qibla of Abraham and the Prophet's birthplace and sanctuary.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المشايخ : إن اليهود استقبلوا القبلة لأن النداء لموسى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others say Christians face the rising lights, while Muslims face Muhammad, the master of lights, from whose light all lights were created.
rows.anchor: وكان بعضهم يقول : استقبلت النصارى مطلع الأنوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kaaba is the earth's center, so directing prayer there symbolizes the duty of justice in all things.
rows.anchor: الكعبة سرة الأرض ووسطها ، فأمر الله تعالى جميع خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The change honors Muhammad, whom the Prophet wished for in opposition to the Jews: God says “a qibla you are pleased with,” suggesting He seeks Muhammad's pleasure in both worlds, as 93:5 promises.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل قبلة أرضاها ، والإشارة فيه كأنه تعالى قال : يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi links the command not to dismiss the poor in 6:52 with this honor: the Kaaba is the direction of Muhammad's face and the poor the direction of God's mercy, so turning away from either is wrongful.
rows.anchor: الكعبة قبلة وجهك ، والفقراء قبلة رحمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes a hierarchy of qiblas: the Throne for its bearers, the Kursi for the pious, the Frequented House for scribes, the Kaaba for believers, and God for bewildered believers (2:115).
rows.anchor: وثامنها : العرش قبلة الحملة ، والكرسي قبلة البررة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the Throne is made of light, the Kursi of pearl, and the Frequented House of ruby; the Kaaba is made from five named mountains, and pilgrimage or prayer toward it expiates sins as heavy as those mountains.
rows.anchor: وثبت أن العرش مخلوق من النور ، والكرسي من الدر ، والبيت المعمور من الياقوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After listing these possible explanations for designating a qibla, al-Razi says the first is the soundest account.
rows.anchor: فهذا جملة الوجوه المذكورة في هذا الباب ، والتحقيق هو الأول

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Sunnis answer the objection to changing directions by holding that God's rulings need no explanation through wisdoms or purposes.
rows.anchor: على قول أهل السنة : إنه لا يجب تعليل أحكام الله تعالى بالحكم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila say directions may have different benefits: a person who regards Abraham's building of the Kaaba as honored may face it with greater reverence and humility.
rows.anchor: إذا ترسخ في أوهام بعض الناس أن هذه الجهات أشرف من غيرها بسبب أن هذا البيت بناه الخليل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They say the Kaaba's construction helped bring about the rise of Arab power, strengthening Arabs' desire to honor it.
rows.anchor: لما كان بناء هذا البيت سببا لظهور دولة العرب كانت رغبتهم في تعظيمه أشد

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They say Jews taunted Muslims for facing Jerusalem, claiming they had taught them the qibla; this disturbed concentration, so a change would restore humility and devotion.
rows.anchor: وذلك مخل بالخضوع والخشوع

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They say the Kaaba is Muhammad's birthplace; honoring it honors him, making people more receptive to his religious commands, so changing the qibla serves a desired end.
rows.anchor: أن الكعبة منشأ محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They explain the change as a test of who follows the Messenger: Jerusalem distinguished Muslims from polytheists in Mecca, while the Kaaba distinguished them from Jews in Medina.
rows.anchor: فأمرهم الله تعالى حين كانوا بمكة أن يتوجهوا إلى بيت المقدس ليتميزوا عن المشركين

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila define guidance as direction that leads the servant to what is best; the straight path leads to Paradise for those who follow it.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : إنما هي الدلالة الموصلة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Al-Razi's Ashʿari school rejects guidance as mere invitation or indication, since both are general to all accountable people; it must mean God's creation of knowledge, making guidance and misguidance God's acts.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا : هذه الهداية إما أن يكون المراد منها الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simile particle in “thus” has five proposed referents: God's guidance; Abu Muslim's middle qibla; Abraham's selection in 2:130; God's honorific choice of this community just as He chose a qibla from His owned directions; or God's famous, extraordinary act of making them a middle community.
rows.anchor: الكاف في { كذالك } كاف التشبيه ، والمشبه به أي شيء هو ؟

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads the comparison as: just as God guided you to the middle qibla, He made you a middle community.
rows.anchor: قول أبي مسلم تقريره كما هديناكم إلى قبلة هي أوسط القبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi proposes that “thus” compares the community's special favor with God's honorific selection of a qibla from directions otherwise equally His property; this grace was not owed.
rows.anchor: خص بعضها بمزيد التشريف والتكريم بأن جعله قبلة فضلا منه وإحسانا فكذلك العباد كلهم مشتركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun can refer to a familiar but unstated antecedent, as “We sent it down” does in 97:1; here it means the marvelous creation of a middle community that only God can accomplish.
rows.anchor: أنه قد يذكر ضمير الشيء وإن لم يكن المضمر مذكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When wasaṭ is a noun it takes the full vowel in ummatan wasaṭan; used adverbially, as in “I sat amid the people,” its middle vowel is lightened.
rows.anchor: والظرف مخفف تقول : جلست وسط القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation of wasaṭ is just, supported by 68:28, where awsaṭ means fairest.
rows.anchor: أن الوسط هو العدل والدليل عليه الآية والخبر والشعر والنقل والمعنى

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal transmits from Sufyan, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, that the Prophet explained “middle community” to mean just; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: القفال عن الثوري عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أمة وسطا قال عدلا )

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying “the best of matters is their middle” is interpreted to mean their most just point.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( خير الأمور أوسطها ) أي أعدلها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is described as the most central in lineage among Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أوسط قريش نسبا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's instruction to follow the middle pattern is also cited as evidence for the just or balanced sense.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( عليكم بالنمط الأوسط )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi cites a line attributed just before this segment to Zuhayr: the community stands in the middle and people approve its judgment in grave times, supporting the sense of justice.
rows.anchor: هم وسط يرضى الأنام بحكمهم … إذا نزلت إحدى الليالي العظائم

rows.speaker: الجوهري، الأخفش، الخليل، قطرب
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari in al-Sihah, along with al-Akhfash, al-Khalil, and Qutrub, glosses ummah wasaṭan as a just community.
rows.anchor: الجوهري في ( الصحاح ) : { وكذالك جعلناكم أمة وسطا } أي عدلا وهو الذي قاله الأخفش والخليل وقطرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasaṭ literally means distance from both ends; since excess and deficiency are bad, the person balanced in character avoids both extremes and is virtuous.
rows.anchor: أن الوسط حقيقة في البعد عن الطرفين ولا شك أن طرفي الإفراط والتفريط رديئان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Justice is called middle because it does not lean toward either litigant, just as a balanced person does not lean to either side.
rows.anchor: العدل هو المعتدل الذي لا يميل إلى أحد الطرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the community middle is praise: a community chosen as witness, with the Messenger as witness over it, must be praised for justice.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن المراد بقوله : ( وسطا ) ما يتعلق بالمدح في باب الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The midpoint relates equally to all sides and is protected, while the ends quickly suffer defect; thus the middle symbolizes balance without bias.
rows.anchor: أن أعدل بقاع الشيء وسطه ، لأن حكمه مع سائر أطرافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation says wasaṭ means the best part of anything, which al-Razi considers preferable to “just.”
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أن الوسط من كل شيء خياره قالوا : وهذا التفسير أولى من الأول

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari cites a Bedouin in Mecca renting a camel for pilgrimage who asks for the finest coins; because objects can be called wasaṭ, “best” may fit better than justice.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : اكتريت جملا من أعرابي بمكة للحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best-of-all-things sense matches 3:110, which calls the community the best brought forth for people.
rows.anchor: أنه مطابق لقوله تعالى : { كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation says that “the middle of us in lineage” means the most virtuous, like a necklace's centerpiece: followers gather around their leader.
rows.anchor: أن الرجل إذا قال : فلان أوسطنا نسبا فالمعنى أنه أكثر فضلا
